questions.question: Define work, energy and power with their SI units.
questions.solution:
**Work:** The work done by a force $F$ acting on a body through a displacement $s$ in the direction of the force is
$$W = Fs\cos\theta = F \cdot s$$
Work is a **scalar** and its SI unit is the **joule (J)**, where $1\ \text{J} = 1\ \text{N m}$.

**Energy:** The capacity of a body to do work is called energy. Its SI unit is also the **joule**, and $1\ \text{J} = 1\ \text{N m} = 1\ \text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-2}$. Energy is also a scalar and its dimensions are $[ML^2T^{-2}]$.

**Power:** The rate of doing work is called power.
$$P = \frac{W}{t} = \frac{F s}{t} = F v$$
Its SI unit is the **watt (W)**, where $1\ \text{W} = 1\ \text{J s}^{-1} = 1\ \text{V A}$.
questions.knowledgeNote: Work is force times displacement, energy is the capacity to do work, and power is the rate of doing work.
